title: setup_zram/setup_zswap repair a stale grub.cfg and fail loudly when the next boot cannot match
objective: A rerun of either swap setup script heals a run cut off between the /etc/default/grub write and grub-mkconfig, stays byte-identical when everything already matches, and exits 1 before touching live swap when grub.cfg or a systemd-boot entry still would not boot the target zswap words.
acceptance_criteria: GRUB defaults on the target, grub.cfg on the old setup: the target's script exits 0 and every grub.cfg linux line carries exactly the target zswap words; the next boot runs the target only
grub.cfg already matching: no grub-mkconfig run, boot files and grub.cfg mtime unchanged, nothing reported as changed
grub.cfg still wrong after the rebuild, or a loader entry with no options line carrying the words: exit 1 naming the line or entry, no swapoff, zswap enabled unchanged
out_of_scope: The host (systemd-boot, no derived file): no host runs or reboots
verifier: bash linux_configuration/fixes/lib/tests/test_swap_switch.sh; vmbox_swap.sh stale-zram|stale-zswap|again|noopts in a fresh BIOS/GRUB guest; pre-commit run --files <changed-files>
